expert_role: City of Vancouver transportation and development engineering reviewer (gatekeeper and source auditor) for packet P09, Mobility, traffic and servicing

findings.issue: Even if the data sprint succeeds, the main driver of every downstream number has no source. Office trips come from 'Floor area per employee' (source_ids: []) and 'Trip rate per person, unit or room' (resident rates only, from a dashboard nobody has read). Neither is a 7 Nov sprint deliverable. On at least 103,200 m2 of non-residential GFA, M01 office and retail trips, and with them M02 demand, M04 flows, M05 kerb demand and M07, stay SCENARIO on 30 Nov. Sprint owners are still roles ('owners are roles; the two students enter their names in the canvas manifest'). Nobody is accountable for the 31 Oct and 7 Nov packs, which are 10 and 17 days away.
findings.fix: Put names, not roles, on every sprint line today. Add two 7 Nov deliverables: (a) a sourced office employment-density row (m2 GFA per job, with source, year and basis) and (b) person-trip rates per employee, dwelling, hotel room and retail m2, each with a source or an explicit 'SCENARIO on 30 Nov' entry in the status strip. Add a 7 Nov go/no-go rule: any pack not two-person checked by then ships as SCENARIO, with no partial green.

findings.issue: ParkingDemandEstimate is defined as 'auto-driver commuters x occupancy'. That gives persons, not vehicles, and overstates stall demand by about 17-28% (occupancy 1.17-1.28). Separately, method step 4 ('Auto-driver trips = auto-person trips / occupancy') double-handles occupancy whenever the loaded share row already splits auto driver from auto passenger. Census journey-to-work and the Trip Diary both report driver and passenger separately. The error passes into M02, M07 and the parking line chart.
findings.fix: Set ParkingDemandEstimate = auto-driver vehicle arrivals x peak accumulation (share parked at once), with no occupancy multiplier. Apply occupancy only when a row carries a combined 'auto' share, and store a row flag driver_passenger_split true/false so the tool picks the correct path. Add a unit test for both paths.

findings.issue: The spec says 'The Trip Diary samples households by residence, so it cannot give workplace-attraction splits', and S16 says 'No destination-based Trip Diary product is listed'. Both are wrong. The diary covers the whole region, so trips by all residents can be tabulated by destination. The 2011 Trip Diary Analysis Report on the same TransLink page publishes 'Weekday Mode Share to Sub-Regions' (Figure 3.X.5c, p.33) by destination sub-region. The real limits are coarse geography (Vancouver/UEL, not CBD), sample size and vintage, not the sampling basis.
findings.fix: Rewrite the limit and the r1 flag detail: residence-weighted region-wide diaries can produce destination-end tabulations, with sample-size caveats. Add the 2011 Analysis Report as a source and a candidate destination row (coarse, 2011). In the sprint, test whether the 2023 dashboard filters by destination. Keep Census place-of-work as the CBD-scale commute row.

findings.issue: The brief requires a below-grade secondary entrance that connects directly to the station. Yet M03 ships 'by 10 Dec', after the 30 Nov deadline, and the launch-day state puts M03 outside the build. Entrants get no in-tool check of the connection width the brief asks for, even though tier 1 is rated effort S (arithmetic).
findings.fix: Ship a tier-0 M03 by 13 Nov: TSPR 2025 hourly alightings for the proxy station x user entrance share, plus tower transit trips, divided by user clear width, mapped to the walkway scale. Label it 'unverified scale, comfort only, not egress-compliant'. Move platform and line context to v1.

findings.issue: The competition page (architecturecompetitions.com/vancouvertallchallenge) gives a Q&A deadline of 3 Nov 2026, with no answers posted. Several statuses stay 'team-applied' only because applicability is unknown, and the organiser can settle that. Open questions: whether the block is inside the Parking By-law Downtown area for the maximum (s.4.2.5), which existing station or lines the hypothetical neighbouring station stands for, and whether City loading and servicing rules are expected. The spec does not use this channel.
findings.fix: Submit those three questions by 3 Nov (role: Student 1). Record the answers as source S64 with date. Raise applicability_status to source-stated wherever an answer confirms it, and keep the team-assumption badge where it does not.

findings.issue: There is still no checked by-law row. Every M02 metric except the switched-off minimum test is unverified, and bylaws.vancouver.ca returned HTTP 403 again in this round (sec05.pdf). Loading counts, bay dimensions (8.5x3.0x3.8 m in 2012 versus 10.2x3.4 m in a 2026 extract), bicycle Class A rates (three conflicting sources) and the downtown maximum all rest on search extracts or vendor pages. Teams that size docks and bike rooms now will size them wrongly, and the dock depth feeds STRC and SPAC.
findings.fix: Keep the 7 Nov pack deadline. Until then, set the M02 visualization to grey for every row and show bay envelopes as 'pending Section 5' outlines in SPAC, not as dimensions. After loading, record the consolidation date and SHA-256 on the board's policy-reflection note.

findings.issue: The design-vehicle library (Class B, Class C, City refuse truck) has no fire apparatus. For a 244-305 m supertall, fire-department access and the ladder or pumper turning envelope at the lane and frontage often governs lane geometry and building setbacks more than delivery vehicles do. The spec hands egress to SYST but never hands off fire-vehicle access.
findings.fix: Add a fourth library slot, 'fire apparatus (Vancouver Fire Rescue Services or Building By-law access route)', status unverified until transcribed. Add a SYST hand-off output, FireAccessRoute, and show its swept path greyed out like the other vehicles.

findings.issue: I independently checked the Figure 9 decode and confirm it. The PDF p.14 fills (green CMYK 0.35/0/1/0, yellow 0/0/0.9/0, at-risk separation, red 0/1/1/0) match the printed label positions. For example, at y=482 (row B-) the labels read 'AT RISK, ACCEPTABLE, AT RISK, ACCEPTABLE' for High Street, Office, Tourist and Transport, and no 'AT RISK' label sits in row B for Office. The previous critic's text-based reading is wrong, but the spec still presents it as a live alternative.
findings.fix: Record the critic's reading as a FALSE ASSUMPTION (see false_assumptions). Downgrade the UNVERIFIED flag to 'geometry and label positions agree; 31 Oct visual check outstanding'. Add an explicit rule for Figure 8 band C (21-23 ppmm), which Figure 9 omits (its rows are A, B+, B, B-, C+, C-, D, E).

findings.issue: The NonResidentialGFACheck metric is marked status 'verified', but S63 is opened=false and its URL is the Buildner homepage. That breaks the packet's own rule that 'verified' needs both sourced and current. The competition page itself confirms only the deadline.
findings.fix: Cite the brief file by name, version and date, plus the competition page URL. Re-read the 9.0 FSR clause and record a page number. Until then, display team_assumption.

findings.issue: The status field still carries 'false_assumption_corrected' on several metrics, with displayed_status beside it, so there are two status fields that can disagree. Other metrics (M01 basis check, M03 TfL-underground rule) mark a tool rule as value_status 'sourced'.
findings.fix: Remove status as a display input. Keep corrected_in_round and flag_ref as history, and compute displayed_status only. Give tool rules a separate value_status 'tool rule'.

findings.issue: The spec uses 2023 hourly TSPR values and says 2025 hourly rows 'were not reached'. The 2025 rows exist. Burrard MF 8-9 AM alightings were 4,306 in 2025 against 3,819 in 2023 (+13%). Granville was 3,353 and Waterfront 3,974.
findings.fix: Load 2025 hourly rows as the default baseline and keep 2023 as a comparison. Label MF as 'Monday-Friday average (inferred)'.

findings.issue: The spec calls the 2014 Truck Classification and Dangerous Goods Survey 'not readable'. It downloads directly (about 20.9 MB). It is an AES-encrypted PDF that opens in any browser or reader, so a person can read it. The block is in the agent's tooling, not in the source.
findings.fix: Add a sprint task to read it manually for truck time-of-day profiles and light/heavy splits near the CBD. Use it for the M05 delivery-hour shape, labelled as screenline-type counts, not building rates.

findings.issue: The unresolved item says derived headway tables 'should be computed at run time per user rather than redistributed'. The TransLink terms grant a licence to 'use, reproduce, and redistribute the Data' with the required legend. Run-time download is a valid choice, but it is not required.
findings.fix: Restate this as a design choice (keeps data fresh). Allow cached derived tables if they carry the legend and the feed date.

findings.issue: The 'bad above 37%' cap comes from Spack and Finkelstein, measured against ITE average rates, which are a car-oriented baseline. It is applied to reductions from a same-basis CBD baseline, which mixes bases.
findings.fix: Label the 37% line 'reduction versus ITE suburban rates, not versus a CBD baseline'. Rely on the same-basis observed floor as the binding constraint.

findings.issue: The EV-ready row relies on Memon 2009 ('EV outlets voluntary'). Reviewer knowledge, which I could not verify this round because the web-search budget was exhausted and vancouver.ca returns 403: Vancouver has required energized EV-ready residential stalls in new buildings since about 2019. Treating EV as voluntary would undersize the SYST electrical room.
findings.fix: Mark the EV row 'likely mandatory, rate to load from Section 4' rather than voluntary, and give it a sprint line.

findings.issue: The sprint ends at '30 Nov: submission', but the competition page gives the deadline as 30 Nov 2026 at 23:59 London time, which is 15:59 Pacific.
findings.fix: Set the freeze and export time to 30 Nov 12:00 Pacific in the manifest.

findings.issue: r5py's licence is confirmed as 'GPL-3.0-or-later OR MIT'. It runs on the Java R5 engine, and the spec does not mention the JDK dependency, which matters for a web deployment.
findings.fix: Add the JDK requirement and the version pin to the library entry, or fall back to gtfs_kit and OSMnx isochrones.

false_assumptions.claim: (Previous critic, carried in the r2 flag as an alternative reading.) TfL Figure 9 rates B 'at risk' at peak for Office and Retail, Residential and Transport Interchange, and rates B+ at risk and B unacceptable for Tourist Attraction.
false_assumptions.why_false: The figure's vector fills and the printed label positions both show Office/Retail and Transport Interchange comfortable to B, acceptable at B- and C+, and at risk at the C- row. Residential is acceptable at B and B-. Tourist Attraction matches High Street: acceptable at B, at risk at B-.
false_assumptions.correction: Adopt the spec's geometry decode as the reading. Drop the critic's reading from the flag and keep only the visual confirmation step.
false_assumptions.evidence: https://content.tfl.gov.uk/pedestrian-comfort-guidance-technical-guide.pdf p.14: green fill (CMYK 0.35/0/1/0) spans y 494-550 (rows A to B) in the Office column (x 163-260); yellow spans 457-494 (B-, C+). Text at y=482 (row B-) reads 'AT RISK ACCEPTABLE AT RISK ACCEPTABLE', and at y=450 (row C-) 'AT RISK' x4 for the Office and Transport columns.

false_assumptions.claim: The Trip Diary samples households by residence, so it cannot give workplace-attraction (destination-based) splits, and no destination-based Trip Diary product exists.
false_assumptions.why_false: The diary is region-wide, so trips from every residence sub-region to a destination can be tabulated. TransLink publishes destination-sub-region mode shares in the 2011 Analysis Report.
false_assumptions.correction: Treat destination-end tabulation as valid, subject to sample size and geography. Add the 2011 report as a coarse destination row and test the 2023 dashboard for a destination filter.
false_assumptions.evidence: https://www.translink.ca/-/media/translink/documents/about-translink/customer-service/trip-diary/2011-metro-vancouver-regional-trip-diary--analysis-report.pdf p.33: 'Figure 3.X.5c - Weekday Mode Share to Sub-Regions: this figure illustrates the mode share of the trips originating in the specific sub-region for each of the destination sub-regions'.

false_assumptions.why_false: Auto-driver trips are already vehicles. Multiplying by occupancy returns persons and inflates stall demand by 17-28%.
false_assumptions.correction: Parking demand = auto-driver vehicle arrivals x peak accumulation. Use occupancy only to convert a combined auto-person share into vehicles.
false_assumptions.evidence: Internal arithmetic. S56 (2011 screenline report) defines occupancy as occupants per passenger vehicle, including the driver (1.17 AM to 1.28 PM).

false_assumptions.claim: The 2014 truck survey is not readable because it exceeds the 10 MB fetch limit.
false_assumptions.why_false: The file downloads directly (about 20.9 MB). It is an encrypted PDF that standard readers open, so a person can read it.
false_assumptions.correction: Read it manually in the sprint.

verdict: Round 2 fixed the earlier gate items: Figure 9 is encoded cell by cell, the crossing and width checks are in, k-scaling is dropped, the claimed-deviation test is in, M03 uses a proxy station, the screenline data are in and route directness is added. I independently confirmed the Figure 9 decode from the page geometry; the previous critic's reading was wrong. The spec still cannot be relied on today. No by-law row is checked, sprint owners are roles, the dominant office-trip drivers (m2 per job, trip rates) have no source or deadline, and ParkingDemandEstimate multiplies vehicles by occupancy. The spec also wrongly says the Trip Diary cannot give destination-based shares, and M03 ships after the deadline. These conditions are narrow and dated. Web search was exhausted this round, so this audit used direct fetches only.
